Proof of concept · public data

Inspect smarter: risk-targeting for San Diego food inspections

Independent analysis by Ayan Pendharkar · San Diego County DEH runs ~21,000 routine inspections/yr on a fixed calendar — this ranks them by risk instead.

The evidence (forward-tested, out-of-sample)

Inspect the top 20% by risk → find ~45% of all critical violations (vs 20% by calendar). Tested on 36,543 inspections the model never saw.

Critical violations found ~6 days earlier within the monthly cycle (95% CI 5.8–6.5), 18 days within a quarter — while clean facilities wait under a day longer.

Trained on routine inspections Jan 2023 – Dec 2024; tested on Jan 2025 – Sep 2026 (36,543 inspections the model never saw). All figures above (AUC, gains, days-earlier) come from that held-out test window.

Statistically checked: AUC is stable at 0.73–0.75 across three separate time cutoffs (rolling-origin backtest); the days-earlier estimate carries a bootstrap 95% CI. Full method & code in the repo.

The worklist — who to inspect next, ranked by risk

Every currently-active facility, scored for its next, not-yet-done inspection using its full history to date — the forward-looking queue inspectors would actually work. Sort by risk, then weigh how long since the last visit. Facilities are anonymized; a named list runs internally. This queue uses a model fitted on all routine inspections Jan 2023 – Sep 2026, scoring each facility as of Sep 18, 2026 — the accuracy of that approach is validated out-of-sample in the evidence above.
